concern_results.conclusion: Test 3d now requires exit code 2, the install_visibility_scan_error token, and no install_visibility_not_found. This matches the validate-skill.sh behavior described in the new register row.
The only change outside the register doc is a test-only shim in a temp dir. No production write path, permission check or sanitization control is touched.
The shim now fails based on the arguments Ruby receives, not on a call count. So moving the pre-rg steps around can no longer send the injected failure to the wrong step.

The prior P2 is resolved. If the shim's pattern matched some other Ruby step, the token check would make the test fail instead of passing silently. The packet can't show whether the visibility script contains the matched string, but either way that can only cause a failing test, not a false pass.
Only the test changes and two register rows that update earlier ones. Nothing is added that the request didn't ask for.
Test and doc only, so a plain revert is enough and there is no state to migrate.
Failure messages now include the actual exit code and the full output, which makes failures easier to diagnose.
The register rows name specific test cases and point to validation.md. The packet doesn't contradict any claim in this delta, and none of them overstate what the cited evidence shows.
The shared-gate boundary is covered: a Ruby failure must now produce the exit 2 failure that the test pins down.
This follows the scripts AGENTS.md rule that changes need self-test coverage and must not downgrade failures. The register uses repo-relative paths only and contains no private data.
